hook.line: “$1,000 to anyone who solves the 15 puzzle with 14 and 15 swapped” — so the story was told. But it can never be solved.
hook.say: Welcome to the great escape history of sliding puzzles!

ch.say: It began in a small American town.
p: The 15 puzzle is said to have been devised in the 1870s by Noyes Chapman, postmaster of Canastota, New York.
In 1880 it became a craze in Boston and beyond, spreading to Europe. In Japan, puzzles like “Hakoiri Musume” became favourites.

tl: Chapman is said to devise the 15 puzzle

ch.cap: Only 14 and 15 are reversed — no sequence of slides can fix it
p: You just slide tiles into the empty square.
But because of parity, a position with exactly two tiles swapped can never be solved. Mathematics cracked the mystery.
